clue.text: Detective taking single round, taken out, wasted

parts.note: DI is the abbreviation for Detective Inspector
a lap is one circuit or round of a track
the Roman numeral for one, a single unit
someone taken out on a romantic outing has been dated

explanation.surface: A detective, having one round of drinks, is escorted from the pub completely drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' looks like slang for drunk but means fallen into ruin. 'taking' is only a link; the charade runs in answer order, so the round comes before the single.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a wasted building or estate has decayed through neglect, ruined and run down.

clue.text: Not fit for exercise after endless final

indicators.note: after places the exercise piece behind the trimmed word
endless asks for the word final without its first and last letters

parts.note: PT is physical training, exercise in school

explanation.surface: Someone is too unfit to exercise after a gruelling final match.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something inapt is unsuitable, not fitting for its purpose.

clue.text: Draw around empty easel in rising artist's studio

indicators.note: in places the drawn-tie unit inside the reversed artist
in a down clue, rising means the artist's letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

indicators.note: around means the draw word wraps the emptied easel

parts.note: a tie is a drawn game

indicators.note: empty strips easel of its inside, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: An artist sketches around an empty easel in a studio, rising to their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' is the verb sketch on the surface but is a noun, a tied game. 'empty' keeps only the outer letters, 'around' wraps, 'in' places, and 'rising' reads upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an atelier is a workshop or studio, especially one used by an artist or designer.

clue.text: Terrain's tilled holding drill

indicators.note: holding says the words Terrain's tilled contain the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: Ground that has been tilled contains a drill hole for planting seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drill' looks like the farmer's seed furrow, fitting the tilled terrain; it means to teach by repetition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to drill a lesson is to instil it by constant repetition.

clue.text: Story from Fitzgerald turned nasty

indicators.note: turned means the singer's first name is read the other way round

parts.note: Ella Fitzgerald was the American jazz singer
gory means bloody, nasty to look at

explanation.surface: A tale by F. Scott Fitzgerald took an unpleasant turn.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitzgerald points to the novelist, but it is the jazz singer Ella.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an allegory is a story whose characters and events carry a hidden moral meaning.

clue.text: Cuts Queen left out of 'Works'

indicators.note: left out of tells us to remove the queen's letters from the works word

parts.note: exercises are pieces of work, tasks or practices
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Edits remove the Queen from a play titled 'Works'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to excise is to cut out or remove a passage or tissue.

clue.text: One provides support for privates?

parts.note: privates suggests underwear or private parts, but means private soldiers, whom an army officer supplies with food, kit and quarters

explanation.surface: It reads like an advert for a supportive undergarment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'privates' tempts a jockstrap reading; the privates are the lowest rank of soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: this army officer is responsible for supplies, stores and accommodation for the troops.

clue.text: Prod underneath stone fish

indicators.note: in a down clue, underneath puts the prod phrase below the stone abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight of fourteen pounds
to urge on is to prod or spur someone

explanation.surface: Someone pokes beneath a rock to find a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prod' is the two-word phrasal verb URGE ON, not a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the sturgeon is a large fish prized for its roe, caviar.

clue.text: Taking gang in critical setting

indicators.note: in places the gang inside the critical word

parts.note: pressing means urgent, critical
a posse is a gang, originally one summoned by a sheriff

explanation.surface: A gang is being taken in during a critical police operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' looks like a verb of capture but is the adjective meaning attractive; 'setting' is a link describing where the gang is placed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: taking can mean charming, and prepossessing means attractive, creating a good impression.

clue.text: Talk posh upset by English etiquette

parts.note: U means upper class, posh

indicators.note: upset turns the talk word upside down, read backwards across

parts.note: to gas is to talk idly

explanation.surface: Someone's affected accent offends an English sense of manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: usage means customary practice, the accepted conventions of behaviour.

clue.text: His employment is sort of brief

definitions.text: His employment is sort of brief

parts.words: His employment is sort of brief
parts.note: brief suggests short-lived work, but a brief is the case papers this lawyer prepares for a barrister

explanation.surface: A man's job is a short-term contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' reads as short, but in British law a brief is the instructions a lawyer gives counsel; a solicitor is the lawyer clients deal with directly.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: this lawyer instructs barristers by preparing briefs, so his work involves that kind of brief.

clue.text: Flogging with belt catching end of huge rump

indicators.note: catching means the belt word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a belt and a ring both encircle something

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of huge

parts.note: the tail is the hind end, the rump

explanation.surface: A beating with a belt lands on the end of a large backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flogging' means selling, not whipping.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: flogging something is selling it, and retailing is selling goods to the public.

clue.text: Paddy field filled by river

indicators.note: filled by means the field word takes the river letter inside

parts.note: in cricket, to field a ball is to stop it

explanation.surface: A rice paddy field is flooded by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy field' is one phrase on the surface; 'Paddy' alone is a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: a paddy is a tantrum, and a strop is a bad-tempered sulk.

clue.text: Rule republic occupied by special army unit

indicators.note: occupied by means the republic is filled by the army unit's letters

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland
MP is the Military Police

explanation.surface: A republic is placed under military rule by a special forces unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: empire means sovereign rule or dominion over territories.

clue.text: 'Country Life' previously not written

parts.note: past means previously, gone by
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A former issue of the magazine Country Life was spoken, not printed.
explanation.walkthrough: Country Life is a British magazine about rural living, but here it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pastoral is a work portraying rural life among shepherds and the countryside.

clue.text: Lewis catching more ruddy crooks!

indicators.note: catching means the author's initials hold the comparative inside

parts.note: C. S. Lewis was the author of the Narnia books
rosier means more red, ruddier

explanation.surface: An exclamation that Lewis has caught some even more ruddy criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooks' suggests villains, but means bishops' staffs; 'ruddy' could be a mild British swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a crosier is the hooked staff a bishop carries, shaped like a shepherd's crook.

clue.text: Favourite's over following raised pace

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the pieces read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a pet is a favourite; the 's adds S
too means excessively, over

explanation.surface: The racing favourite is beaten after a raised pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' applies to the whole string, since in a down clue the letters read upwards; 'over' is excessively, not the cricket over.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pace is a single step, the act of putting one foot forward.

clue.text: Old beast old lady crushed, without love

parts.note: ma is mother, one's old lady

indicators.note: without means the love letter is dropped from the crushed phrase

parts.note: stood on means crushed underfoot
O is love, nil in tennis

explanation.surface: An elderly woman was flattened by an old animal, unloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed' is the phrase STOOD ON; 'without love' takes one O away, leaving STODON.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the mastodon is an extinct elephant-like mammal, a prehistoric beast.

clue.text: Sour face, in wrong place to score!

parts.note: milk that is off has gone sour
a side is a face of a solid object

explanation.surface: A footballer pulls a sour face, caught out of position to score.
explanation.walkthrough: In football, a player is offside when ahead of the last defender as the ball is played, so a goal cannot count.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporting sense: a player offside is positioned illegally, so any goal scored is disallowed.

clue.text: Breather taking oxygen before end of exercise? Relax

indicators.note: before puts the oxygen-filled organ ahead of the final letter
taking means the breather word takes the oxygen symbol inside

parts.note: a lung is the organ one breathes with
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of exercise

explanation.surface: Take a breather and breathe in oxygen before finishing a workout, then relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breather' looks like a rest; it is the lung.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to lounge is to relax lazily, lying or sitting at ease.

clue.text: Perfect work compiler's found in corporation

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: found in places the compiler's contraction inside the corporation word

parts.note: corporation is old slang for a pot belly, a tum
the compiler is the setter, so compiler's means I'm, I am

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter's perfect work is discovered inside a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like a company but is jokey British slang for a large belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: optimum means best or most favourable, ideal and perfect.

clue.text: Land initially next to snake here?

definitions.text: Land initially next to snake here?

indicators.note: next to sets the first letter beside the snake word
initially picks the first letter of Land

parts.note: an adder is a snake, the viper found in Britain

explanation.surface: In a board game, landing next to a snake is where this appears.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue evokes the board game Snakes and Ladders, where landing on a snake sends you down and this takes you up.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: in Snakes and Ladders the board has climbing ladders beside the snakes.

clue.text: 'Dandy' is back containing old joke

indicators.note: containing means the reversed dandy phrase holds the old letter
back means the dandy word and its s are read backwards

parts.note: a fop is a dandy, a man obsessed with clothes
the 's of 'Dandy' is stands for is, giving S

explanation.surface: The Dandy comic is back with an old gag.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dandy was a long-running British children's comic, but here a dandy is a fop.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a spoof is a hoax or parody, a joke played on someone.

clue.text: Delilah was one character taking time cutting hair

indicators.note: cutting means the character piece goes into the hair word

parts.note: a tress is a long lock of hair

indicators.note: taking means the character word takes the time letter inside

parts.note: an air is a manner or character

explanation.surface: Delilah, in character, takes her time cutting Samson's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'taking' puts time inside the character word first, and 'cutting' then drives that unit into the lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Delilah betrayed Samson to the Philistines, making her a treacherous woman.

clue.text: Heartless pride and greed perhaps creating stain

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the pride word is removed

parts.note: ego means self-esteem, pride
greed is one of the seven deadly sins, so an example of sin

explanation.surface: Pride and greed, lacking heart, leave a moral stain.
explanation.walkthrough: Pride and greed both look like deadly sins, but pride is EGO cut to EO.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: eosin is a red dye used to stain tissue samples in microscopy.

clue.text: Like a cadaver returned, one consumed by dead

parts.note: returned is came back, so the word came written back
I is the Roman numeral one
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A corpse brought back, with someone eaten by the dead, horror-film style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' does double duty as 'came back': CAME is written back as EMAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: emaciated means abnormally thin, the gaunt wasted look of a corpse.

clue.text: He played academic chasing child

indicators.note: chasing puts the child after the academic

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, an academic
a son is a child

explanation.surface: An actor once played a professor chasing a young girl.
explanation.walkthrough: James Mason played Humbert Humbert, the academic who pursues a child in Lolita.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: James Mason was a British film actor, so he played many screen roles.

clue.text: Make-up is bait trapping blokes after date

indicators.note: trapping means the bait word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to bait is to lure or tempt

indicators.note: after places the blokes behind the date

parts.note: an era is a date or period
men are blokes

explanation.surface: Cosmetics are used as bait to trap men after a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' suggests cosmetics but means a person's character.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person's make-up is their nature, their temperament or disposition.
